heading: How to Calculate Capital Gains on NPS Tier II Withdrawals
tldr: NPS Tier II is an optional, flexible investment account with no lock-in period, unlike Tier I.
Contributions to NPS Tier II are not eligible for tax deductions under Section 80C.
Withdrawals from NPS Tier II are subject to capital gains tax, depending on the asset class and holding period.
The eNPS portal currently does not provide a consolidated capital gains statement for Tier II accounts.
Investors must maintain meticulous records of their Tier II transactions to accurately calculate taxable gains.
caption:
Thinking of taking money out of your NPS Tier II account? It’s important to know how much tax you might pay. This account is flexible, but calculating your tax on withdrawals can be tricky because you don't get a ready-made statement. Our guide breaks down exactly how to figure out your capital gains tax simply. Read the full article to understand how to keep good records and avoid surprises.
